stories.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong — 44 HR, Still 3 Steals From 40-40

x_posts.label: Post 1
x_posts.text:
Pete Crow-Armstrong went 3-for-4 with TWO home runs (Nos. 43 AND 44) as the Cubs beat Atlanta 8-4.

PCA is now the first Cub EVER with 44 home runs — and just 3 steals from making the 40-40 club.

Historic September. #Cubs

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text:
The 40-40 checklist:

✅ 40 HR — DONE (44 now, first Cub ever)
⬜ 40 SB — 37, need 3 more

About 10 games left. PCA is chasing something no Cub has ever done. #Cubs

facebook.long_form:
Pete Crow-Armstrong is making history one at-bat at a time. ⚾

On Wednesday night, PCA went 3-for-4 with two home runs — Nos. 43 AND 44 — as the Cubs beat the Braves 8-4. In one game, he erased Billy Williams' franchise record for home runs by a left-handed hitter (42, set in 1970) and became the first Cub in franchise history to hit 44 home runs in a season.

The 40-40 side of the ledger: he sits at 37 stolen bases. Needs 3 more. With approximately 10 games left, the math is very much alive.

If PCA gets there, he becomes just the 7th player in MLB history to hit 40 home runs and steal 40 bases in the same season. No Cub has ever done it. The list of players who have — Barry Bonds, Jose Canseco, Alex Rodriguez, Alfonso Soriano, Carlos Beltran, Eric Davis — reads like a power-speed Hall of Fame.

The Cubs hold the NL Wild Card 1 spot at 84-68. Every game matters now — and for Cubs fans, every stolen base attempt will have the whole ballpark holding its breath.
facebook.image_caption: 44 home runs. 37 stolen bases. 3 steals from history. PCA is in the middle of something special. #Cubs

article.headline: PCA Hits Home Runs 43 and 44, Breaks Cubs Franchise Record — 3 Steals From 40-40 Club

stories.title: Brewers Clinch NL Central — 4th Consecutive Title

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
OFFICIAL: The Milwaukee Brewers have clinched the NL Central.

Four consecutive division titles — the first team to win four straight NL Central crowns since the division was created in 1994.

94-57. First to clinch in 2026. #Brewers

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
How the Brewers clinched Tuesday:

✅ Misiorowski: 5 IP, 0 R, 7 K
✅ Final: MIL 5, PIT 1
✅ Cubs lost to Atlanta same night

Jacob Misiorowski — nearly unhittable even on a clinch night. #Brewers

facebook.long_form:
The Milwaukee Brewers have done something no team has done since the NL Central division was created in 1994. 🍺

On Tuesday night, Jacob Misiorowski struck out 7 in 5 shutout innings as the Brewers beat the Pittsburgh Pirates 5-1 at PNC Park. While Milwaukee was handling business in Pittsburgh, the Cubs were losing to Atlanta. When both games ended, the scoreboard math was complete: the Brewers had clinched their fourth consecutive NL Central division title.

Four straight. That has never been done in this division's 32-year history.

The Brewers finished the night at 94-57 — the best record in baseball and the first team in any division to clinch in 2026. They are the NL's No. 1 seed with a first-round bye, and they will be playing October baseball with home-field advantage throughout the NL side of the bracket.

And the pitcher who headlined the clincher? Misiorowski, who has been the best pitcher in baseball this season (19-8, 1.95 ERA, 236 K). He was dominant even on a party night. That's your Cy Young frontrunner.
facebook.image_caption: Four straight NL Central titles. 94-57. First to clinch in 2026. The Brewers are running this division. #Brewers

article.headline: Brewers Clinch Fourth Consecutive NL Central Title — First Team to Win Four Straight Since Division Creation in 1994

stories.title: Yordan Alvarez — Triple Crown Slipping Away

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Yordan Alvarez's Triple Crown math is getting harder:

🔴 HR: 38, trailing Caminero (41) by 3
🔴 RBI: ~96, trailing Alonso (~100) by ~4
🟡 BA: .310, leads AL

Since Aug. 2: .242, 3 HR, 12 RBI. ~10 games left. #Astros

facebook.long_form:
The Triple Crown numbers for Yordan Alvarez heading into the final stretch: 📊

🟡 Batting Average: .310 — leads the American League. This one is still his.
🔴 Home Runs: 38 — trails Junior Caminero (Tampa Bay Rays, 41) by 3.
🔴 RBI: approximately 96 — trails Pete Alonso (Baltimore Orioles, ~100) by approximately 4.

Roughly 10 games remain. The window is closing.

Here's the deeper concern: since August 2, Alvarez has hit just .242 with 3 home runs and 12 RBI over 35 games. That's a 46-game cold stretch that has cost him ground in both the home run and RBI races. He still leads in batting average — but Chandler Simpson (Rays) is within five points.

The last time an American League player won the Triple Crown was Miguel Cabrera in 2012. Alvarez had the best chance since then. Whether it gets done depends on whether he can snap out of his cold stretch in the final 10 games while Caminero and Alonso maintain their leads — a very tall order for a race that's gone from possible to unlikely.
facebook.image_caption: The Triple Crown window is closing for Yordan Alvarez. .310 BA, 38 HR, 96 RBI. With 10 games left, he needs a run. #Astros

article.headline: Yordan Alvarez's Triple Crown Is Slipping: .310 BA, 38 HR, 3 Behind Caminero With 10 Games Left

stories.title: NL Wild Card Race — Cubs Catch Breaks on Sept. 17

x_posts.label: Post 6
x_posts.text:
Cubs WC1 lead growing on Sept. 17 — Phillies, Padres AND D-backs all lost.

Cubs 84-68 | WC1
Phillies 83-68 | WC2, 1.0 back
Padres 82-69 | WC3, 1.5 back

Wild Card starts Sept. 29. #Cubs #MLB

facebook.long_form:
The Cubs needed a favor on Thursday — and they got three of them. ⚾

On September 17, while Chicago waited to see where things stood, the Phillies lost, the Padres lost, AND the Diamondbacks lost. All three Wild Card rivals fell in the same evening. The result: the Cubs' lead in the NL Wild Card 1 race grew to 1.5 games over Philadelphia, with the Padres 1.5 back in WC3.

Here's the NL Wild Card picture with approximately 10 games to play:

🔵 Chicago Cubs: 84-68 — WC1
🔴 Philadelphia Phillies: 83-68 — WC2, 1.0 game back
🟤 San Diego Padres: 82-69 — WC3, 1.5 games back
🔵 Arizona Diamondbacks: 80-72 — 4.0 games back

The Wild Card Series starts September 29. With the Brewers (No. 1 seed, bye), Dodgers (No. 2, bye), and Braves (No. 3) all but locked in, the two remaining NL Wild Card spots belong to whoever holds on in this three-team race over the next 10 days. Cubs fans will have their eyes on the scoreboard every night.
facebook.image_caption: Phillies, Padres and Diamondbacks all lost Thursday. Cubs WC1 lead growing. 10 games to play. #Cubs #MLB

article.headline: NL Wild Card Race: Cubs Catch Breaks as Phillies, Padres and Diamondbacks All Lose Sept. 17

stories.title: Aaron Judge — New Injury Scare, Yankees Managing for October

x_posts.label: Post 7
x_posts.text:
Aaron Judge left Wednesday's game vs. Minnesota in the 6th inning with right lower-leg tightness.

He had just returned Sept. 8 from a 99-day IL stint. No timetable announced.

Yankees protecting their guy for October. #Yankees

facebook.long_form:
The Yankees caught a scare Wednesday night — and now the October countdown has a health question mark attached. ⚾

Aaron Judge left the team's game against the Minnesota Twins in the sixth inning with right lower-leg tightness. He had been 0-for-2 with two strikeouts when manager Aaron Boone lifted him for pinch-hitter Heliot Ramos. Judge said he noticed the discomfort in the first inning while playing the field. Boone's assessment: "Hopefully it's something we were able to catch." No timetable for a return was announced.

Here's the context that makes this story significant: Judge returned from a fractured right rib just nine days ago on September 8. He had missed all of June, July, and August — a 99-day IL stint. He played fewer than 10 days at full health before a new injury sent him to the bench.

The Yankees have already clinched their 61st postseason berth (ninth in 10 seasons). They are not playing for anything in these final two weeks except to have their best player healthy for October. With the Wild Card beginning September 29, the organization's posture is clear: protect Judge. The risk of losing him for the postseason entirely outweighs any regular-season benefit. Whether this becomes a serious concern or a short-term maintenance issue will define the Yankees' October ceiling.
facebook.image_caption: Aaron Judge exits Wednesday's game with lower-leg tightness. He just came back 9 days ago. Yankees managing him for October. #Yankees

article.headline: Aaron Judge Exits With Lower-Leg Tightness — Yankees Managing Their Star for October After 99-Day Absence
